first_impression.reaction: My assistant flagged it, so I gave it the first screen. It's calm and it doesn't try to sell me a ring, which I respect. But the ring is with our family jeweller, not a blog. Her summary would be one line: 'tasteful style guide, nothing about planning at our scale.' I skimmed down to the end to see who wrote it and what they do.

journey.quote: No grading tables, no prices, no rules. Just proportion, preference and light.
journey.reaction: Good. Quiet, no price talk, no 'value'. This reads like a magazine, not a shop.

journey.quote: Most couples arrive at the jeweller knowing they want a diamond and little else.
journey.reaction: That isn't me, and it tells me who this was written for. Fine for most readers. Not a reason for me to stay.

journey.section: How to try engagement ring cuts on
journey.quote: If a mock-up is offered, wear it for a day before deciding.
journey.reaction: Sensible, but it's written for someone in a showroom with a sales assistant. Ours comes to the house.

journey.section: From the ring to the destination
journey.quote: When you are ready to plan, Wedded Concierge looks after venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, with one Wedded Advisor as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: This is the only line that's about us. 'Single point of contact' is the right idea. But there's nothing about guest numbers in the hundreds, closing a property, security or keeping things private. 'Venue, travel, vendors and payments' sounds like it could be anyone's wedding.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor is happy to talk it through, from the first idea onwards.
journey.reaction: A little eager. I don't need anyone to be happy to talk. I need to know they've done this before, at this size, without it ending up on Instagram.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Concierge delivered weddings of 200 to 400 guests with VIP logistics?
Can they arrange exclusive use of a property and work alongside our own security team?
How do they handle privacy: NDAs, vendor confidentiality, no social media from staff?
Is there a private or referral channel, rather than a public enquiry form?

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor is happy to talk it through, from the first idea onwards.
turn_offs_found.why: Slightly eager service tone. Minor, but it's the last thing on the page.

cta_reaction.quote: You can talk to a Wedded Concierge about a proposal or wedding abroad.
cta_reaction.why: A ring-shape article isn't how we choose a planner, and a public link isn't how we enquire. Nothing here shows scale or discretion. If someone we trust recommended them, my assistant might look at the concierge page. This post wouldn't be the reason.

top_3_changes: In the concierge paragraph, add one understated line that shows they can handle large guest lists, exclusive use and private arrangements, if that is true. Right now it reads like a standard service.
Offer a discreet, private way to get in touch (a direct advisor contact or by referral) as well as the general link.
Make the closing line calmer and less eager, e.g. drop 'is happy to'.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes an exact sentence from the draft
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, assistant-led, discretion-first)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments and image slots treated as invisible
No problems invented: tone and no-price framing noted as positives

assumptions: Persona is provisional (not CRM-calibrated). The low relevance score is mostly a topic mismatch (ring-shape guide vs. planner shortlisting), not a flaw in the draft.
